title: Chemnitz: no fight over words if Fathers teach reconciliation rightly
source_text: XXXI. Neque etiam, modo quis fateatur remissionem peccatorum nostrorum omnino gratuitam esse, & in solo Christi merito fundatam, nec ullam esse piorum justitiam & opera bona, quae possint ferre severum & rigidum judicii divini examen, crimen esse existimant, si quis ita extendat vocem justificationis, ut internam nostram renovationem sub ea complectatur. Agnoscunt enim a Patribus vocem istam saepius hoc sensu usurpatam esse, nec tamen iis propterea litem movendam censent. Sic enim loquitur Chemnitius in Examine Concilii Tridentini, Nequaquam tales sumus turbatores, qui verae & solidae, & salutaris concordiae ita simus iniqui, & adeo cupidi contentionum, ut etiamsi de rebus ipsis constituta esset pia & salutaris consensio, quaesituri tamen essemus materiam rixarum, ex verborum pugnis. Patribus enim, licet plerunque verbum justificare accipiant pro renovatione, qua efficiuntur in nobis per Spiritum opera justitiae, non movemus litem, ubi juxta Scripturam recte & commode tradunt, quomodo & quare persona Deo reconcilietur, acceptat remissionem peccatorum & adoptionem, & acceptetur ad vitam aeternam. In Exam. Conc. Trid. de Justif. pag. 129.
pass_a_gloss: Nor do they think it a crime, provided someone confesses that the remission of our sins is altogether gratuitous and founded in the merit of Christ alone, and that there is no righteousness of the pious and no good works that can bear the severe and rigid examination of the divine judgment, if someone so extends the word of justification that it embraces our inward renewal under it. For they acknowledge that this word was often used by the Fathers in this sense, and yet they do not think a quarrel should be moved against them on that account. For thus Chemnitz speaks in the Examination of the Council of Trent: By no means are we such disturbers, who are so unfair to true and solid and saving concord, and so eager for contentions, that even if a pious and saving agreement were established concerning the things themselves, we would still seek matter for quarrels from fights about words. For with the Fathers, although they for the most part take the verb to justify for the renewal by which works of righteousness are wrought in us by the Spirit, we do not move a quarrel where according to Scripture they rightly and conveniently hand down how and why a person is reconciled to God, receives remission of sins and adoption, and is accepted unto eternal life. In Exam. Conc. Trid. de Justif. p. 129.
pass_b_english: If remission is free in Christ's merit alone, extending justify to cover inward renewal is no crime.
Chemnitz: no word-fights with Fathers who rightly teach reconciliation, remission, adoption.

choices.why: Wider lexical scope without dogmatic betrayal.
